themes.theme_title: Further use of Maps; Introduction to the rest of Africa

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should be able to use large scale maps or ‘survey’ maps to find out and describe more about areas.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand what a contour is (u)
use contours to describe the relief of an area (s)
recognise physical and other features on conventional survey maps and photographs (s)
use contours to show physical features on maps and draw cross-sections from simple contour maps (s)
understand how to use a survey map to find out about the geography of an area (u)
use survey maps to describe the relief, drainage, vegetation, farming, settlements, transport and other human activities of an area (s)
use a sketch map to show the areas on a map (s)
appreciate the usefulness of survey maps in studying Geography (a, gs)

must_cover: Describing an area from a survey map

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners go outside in an area with different kinds of slopes. Ask learners to line up along a contour and another group to line up along a contour above or below the first one to show what a contour is. Choose an area of steep slopes and an area of gentler slopes. Ask learners to stand on one contour and others to stand on contours above and below. Explain that on a steep slope contours are close together and a gentle slope far apart.

Use a place with a small valley, hill and spur. Or use a sand tray to show these. Learners line up along contours, or mark on sand tray, contours around the hill, valley and spur to show the shape of these features on contour map.
Use a very simple contour map showing steep and gentle slopes, valley, hill, spur, flat land etc. with questions to help learners to recognise features.

Use survey maps for learners to describe relief, physical features, drainage, vegetation, farming, settlement, transport and other human activities in an area. Ask questions to relate human features to physical features and to each other.
To help with this, learners practise using sketch maps to show the areas on a map and use maps in local area fieldwork.
Learners describe the economic development of an area, using a survey map, including problems facing development and prospects for development.
Learners practise drawing cross sections and showing physical and human features on these.
Compare hand-drawn landscape profiles with those that can be drawn digitally e.g. using Google Earth

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In conversation, ask learners to use their maps to explain what contours show and explain what kind of shapes different contour patterns mean in the landscape.
Ask learners to describe physical features and human features seen on a survey map and relate the two. Observe how accurate their descriptions are of these features.
Provide learners with exercises to draw cross sections of physical features. They should mark features on them and relate these to height. Observe the accuracy of their work.
Observe learners use of maps to explain features in the landscape and patterns of development.

practicals.title: Contour demonstration
practicals.description_verbatim: Learners go outside in an area with different kinds of slopes. Ask learners to line up along a contour and another group to line up along a contour above or below the first one to show what a contour is

suggested_uses: Compare hand-drawn landscape profiles with those that can be drawn digitally e.g. using Google Earth

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should know the size of Africa compared with other continents, its position in the world and the size and position of East Africa within Africa.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the position of Africa in the world (k)
know the size of Africa compared to other continents (k)
know the position and size of East Africa within Africa (k)
understand that Africa occupies a unique position as the most tropical of continents (u)
understand the characteristics of important kinds of physical features in Africa and East Africa, including mountain ranges, volcanoes, plateaus, basins and rift valleys (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Use globes, a wall map and atlas maps of the world. Learners describe the position of Africa compared to other continents and to the equator and tropics. Show learners different map projections in 2D maps and notice the relative size appearance of Africa. Compare with the size shown on a globe.
Use a table to show the areas of each continent and challenge learners to construct a simple bar graph or pie chart to represent these. They should compare the size of Africa with other continents.
OR learners make a table of the areas of continents from the Internet and compare the sizes with Africa.
Use a wall map and atlas maps of Africa or Internet maps for learners to describe the position of East Africa within Africa and the comparative size of East Africa.
Draw a sketch map of Africa, showing major features.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In conversation, ask learners to explain where the continent of Africa is in the world with reference to world geometry and identify some of its characteristics associated with this location.
In conversation, ask learners to explain why Africa appears to have a different relative size on some 2D maps.
Ask learners to write an essay about what makes Africa different from other continents. Assess to what extent this essay reflects they key issues learnt from this topic.

suggested_uses: Learners make a table of the areas of continents from the Internet and compare the sizes with Africa.
Use Internet maps for learners to describe the position of East Africa

topic_metadata.topic_title: THE RELIEF REGIONS AND DRAINAGE OF AFRICA

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should know the relief regions of Africa, the major landforms and drainage and understand how they were formed and the effects of these on development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the names and positions of the major relief regions of Africa (k)
recognise physical features from photographs (s)
draw diagrams to show the formation of important physical features (s)
understand the characteristics of important kinds of physical features in Africa and East Africa, including mountain ranges, volcanoes, plateaus, basins and rift valleys (u)
understand the main concepts of plate tectonics and how this has led to the formation of the main physical features of Africa and East Africa (u)
draw a sketch map to show the major relief regions, rivers and lakes (s)
understand how different landforms affect the lives of people living in these communities (u)
appreciate that many areas contain very old rocks not very good for soil formation but rich in minerals (a)
realise that volcanic areas are the most fertile in Africa (u)
understand the effects of the landforms on development, including agriculture and mining (u)
locate the main rivers and lakes of Africa (s)
understand the importance of rivers and lakes for development (u)
appreciate that rivers and lakes can be useful but can as also be spoilt by pollution (a, gs)
understand how their own lives and the lives of their communities are affected by physical features, including natural hazards (u)
understand through case studies how the physical features affect the lives of people in selected areas of East Africa (u)
study through field work any of the above physical features in the local area (s)
understand how water resources are used and controlled (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners work in groups to research and create their own 2D or 3D maps, adding features as they learn about them.
Use a wall map and atlas map or Internet map showing relief of Africa and images, including aerial images. Learners locate and describe the position of the main mountain areas of Africa.
Look up Drakensburg and Atlas Mountains on Internet and make notes about their origins
Use modelling techniques and diagrams to explain folded mountains: Atlas Mountains.
Learners develop their maps, devising their own key to show regions and features they have investigated and learnt about.
Use an atlas, wall map or Internet map to identify main rivers and lakes of Africa. Learners add these features to their own maps.
Learners create a case study of an area where agriculture or mining has thrived and explain how landforms have influenced people’s way of life there.
Learners investigate the local area through fieldwork and map the key landforms and development, making connections between the two.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe as learners use their maps to discuss the advantages of Africa’s landforms and relief features for the development of Africa and make connections. (Answers should mention areas of good volcanic soils with high population densities; areas of minerals e.g. copper, gold, uranium; fertile sedimentary soils and oil deposits; mountains good for tourism)

Learners use evidence from their case studies to present and identify some of the advantages and problems caused by landforms and how this has affected communities. Observe the extent to which learners are able to describe key advantages and problems.
Observe as learners discuss findings from their fieldwork and interpret their local area.

practicals.title: Local area fieldwork on landforms and development
practicals.description_verbatim: Learners investigate the local area through fieldwork and map the key landforms and development, making connections between the two.

suggested_uses: Use Internet map showing relief of Africa and images, including aerial images.
Look up Drakensburg and Atlas Mountains on Internet

topic_metadata.topic_title: THE CLIMATE AND VEGETATION OF AFRICA

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should understand the distribution of climates in Africa and the reasons for them, and the effect of these climates on human development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the relationship between the Earth and the Sun and how this affects temperatures and seasons (u)

draw diagrams to show the relationship between the Earth and the Sun’s rays and the causes of temperature variations and use these to show why the Earth can be divided into tropical, temperate and polar regions (s)
understand the characteristics of the climates of Africa and factors influencing them (u)
appreciate that people’s lifestyles are influenced by the type of weather and climate (a)
understand through case studies how selected climates and types of vegetation affect the way of life of the people in those areas (u)
appreciate that the differences in the ways of life and cultures of people are partly a product of the different climates (a)
draw a map showing the climates and vegetation of East Africa
draw climate graphs of local and other areas and describe climates using these
appreciate that the traditional way of life and farming of all people of Africa is strongly influenced by the climates (a, gs)
appreciate that modern technologies and urbanisation have made people less dependent on the climate. (a, gs)
understand through field work the characteristics of the vegetation and how vegetation is affected by the climates (u)
form opinions about the dangers of the overuse of the natural vegetation (a)
appreciate the need to love and care for their local area, community and country by replanting the vegetation and carry this out (a/ s)
understand the main characteristics of the climates and how each affects the vegetation of the area (u)
understand how the traditional farming and way of life was influenced by the climate (u)

must_cover: Factors affecting the climates of Africa
Effects of climate on way of life

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners look up Inter-tropical Convergence Zone on Internet and find out about its position, seasonal movements and effects.
Give climate statistics for learners to draw climate graphs for each kind of climate in Africa: equatorial, savannah, desert, Mediterranean.
Learners draw sketch map showing these climates in Africa
Learners look up on the Internet each of the above climates in Africa and find the positions and climates of each.
Learners investigate the effects of climate on livelihoods through local scale case studies, comparing these to identify some key positive and negative factors.
Show photographs of each of the climatic regions or use the Internet to find photographs. Learners to decide, with reasons, which climatic region is being shown.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe as learners use maps and diagrams to explain the distribution of climate patterns across the continent of Africa, with explanations for difference and making connections with factors such as latitude, altitude, and time of year.
Observe as learners compare two of the climatic regions of Africa, mentioning climate, causes of the climate, and the effect of the climates on the way of life.
In conversation, ask learners to reflect and suggest whether people in Africa today are less affected by the climates than they were traditionally.

Ask learners to use their work to explain some of the current and future challenges people face from climate, and give examples (including the effect of climate change), Observe their work to check for understanding.

practicals.title: Local scale case studies on climate and livelihoods
practicals.description_verbatim: Learners investigate the effects of climate on livelihoods through local scale case studies, comparing these to identify some key positive and negative factors.

suggested_uses: Learners look up Inter-tropical Convergence Zone on Internet
Learners look up on the Internet each of the above climates in Africa and find the positions and climates of each.
Use the Internet to find photographs

themes.theme_title: Introduction to the Rhine lands and China; agriculture in Africa

topic_metadata.topic_title: EUROPE: THE RHINELANDS: LOCATION, RELIEF REGIONS, DRAINAGE AND CLIMATE

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should know the location of the Rhinelands within Europe and its relief regions, drainage and climate.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know why there is an area called the Rhinelands (k)
know the location of the Rhinelands and the countries within it (k)
locate places on an atlas map using latitude and longitude and describe the places from information on the map (s)
know the names of the main areas of relief and rivers (k)
understand how the river Rhine links these areas together (u)
use and interpret symbols and identify features on a map using a key (s)
use maps to show the major transport routes (s)
understand the role of the different types of transport in development (u)
draw climate graphs of local and other areas and describe climates using these (s)
draw maps to show the areas of the case studies and graphs to illustrate their climates (s)
appreciate why it is useful for Ugandans to study the Rhinelands (a, gs)
appreciate that people’s lifestyles are influenced by the type of weather and climate (a)

must_cover: Location, relief and drainage of Rhinelands

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners use Internet to look up Rhine River and find out which countries it flows through.
Ask learners to draw their own sketch map of the Rhinelands area, using a key.
Use two climate graphs of Rhinelands areas: one on upper Rhine, one on lower Rhine. Ask learners, as a class to describe the climate of each, mentioning similarities and differences.
Learners use the Internet to look up conflicts between Germany and France.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe as learners use their maps to describe a journey down the Rhine valley from Switzerland to Netherlands, mentioning the relief of the area on the way, the countries, the languages and the main towns.
Learners use their work to explain similarities and difference between the climates of the places studied and give some ideas as to why this might be.

suggested_uses: Learners use Internet to look up Rhine River
Learners use the Internet to look up conflicts between Germany and France

topic_metadata.topic_title: INTRODUCTION TO CHINA: LOCATION, SIZE, RELIEF REGIONS, DRAINAGE AND CLIMATE

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should understand the importance of China, its location, size, relief regions, and climate.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: use a world map to locate each country (China)
locate places on an atlas map, using latitude and longitude and describe the places from information on the map (s)
use maps, statistics, graphs and diagrams to analyse population (s)
know the size of China in area and population(k)
use statistics to compare the population of China with other major countries and East Africa (s)
understand the importance of China in the world (u)
understand the differences between the main regions of China (u)
understand the trade patterns of the selected countries and the factors influencing them (u)
draw maps to show the areas of the case studies and graphs to illustrate their climates (s)
recognise physical features from photographs (s)
know the main regions of China (k)
appreciate the importance of learning about China (a, gs)
draw climate graphs of local and other areas and describe climates using these (s)

must_cover: Relief and Climatic Regions of China

suggested_learning_activities.description: Present a table comparing the size and population of China with other major countries of the world and East Africa: China, India, USA, Russia. Ask questions to compare the population and area of China with the other countries. Initially, challenge learners to work in groups to match a population statistic with the correct country. Learners then research the answers and check their work.
Show photographs and learners guess which area each comes from or use photographs from the Internet.
Learners work in groups to produce a large sketch map showing the main regions of China, using atlases and digital maps to guide them.
Learners look up monsoon on Internet.
Learners collaborate to produce a ‘weather forecast’ for a given reason, using maps and charts and present it to the rest of the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners use maps and atlases to describe location, using appropriate vocabulary and terminology.
Observe learners explain the population statistics they have compiled with each other and any adjustments they make.
Observe learners as they discuss their answers with each other. How well are they using evidence to support their answers?
Observe as learners use their own maps and graphs to explain the relief and varying climates of China.
Observe as: learners explain their forecast using their maps and charts; explain type of expected weather using climate as a reference point.

suggested_uses: Discuss learners’ perceptions and any differences in data found on the Internet.
Use photographs from the Internet
Using atlases and digital maps to guide them
Learners look up monsoon on Internet

topic_metadata.topic_title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURE IN AFRICA

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the main types of agriculture in Uganda and the rest of East Africa and the factors influencing them (u)
understand how agriculture in Africa is influenced by the climate (u)
understand how the traditional farming and way of life was influenced by the climate (u)
appreciate the importance of land and water as a source of food, livelihood and income for families, clans and communities (a)
form opinions about the dangers of overuse of land and water resources and the need to conserve these in the local area
appreciate that caring for and preserving resources in the local environment, community and country are signs of love for one’s country
know the main subsistence and commercial crops and main animals kept (k)
know the main pastoral farming areas in Africa (k)
understand the differences between traditional pastoral farming and modern ranching (u)
understand the similarities in traditional agriculture in East Africa and the rest of Africa(u)
understand the change from subsistence agriculture to commercial agriculture (u)
understand the advantages and disadvantages of smallholdings and plantations (u)
understand the importance of agriculture in the economies of African countries (u)
understand the main features of nomadic pastoral farming (u)
understand problems of nomadic farming adjusting to the modern economy (u)
understand the advantages and disadvantages of commercial ranching (u)
understand the conflicts between pastoralists and arable farmers (u)
draw maps to show typical farms in Africa (s)
recognise and describe types of agriculture in Africa from photographs (s)
describe the climate of a pastoral farming area from a climate graph (s)
draw a map to show the main pastoral farming areas of Africa (s)
draw a summary table comparing nomadic pastoral farming with commercial ranching (gs, gs)
appreciate the importance of agriculture in African economies and the need to improve agriculture (a, gs)
appreciate the difficulties of pastoralists adapting to a modern way of living (a, gs)
using photographs, understand how and why the way of life is changing (u)

must_cover: Traditional agriculture in East Africa and Africa
Conflict between nomadic pastoral farming and arable farmers

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners find a case study of cocoa farming in Ghana on Internet.
Support learners to locate areas where cocoa is grown in Ghana and create a map to show this.
Support learners to locate and map rubber plantations in Liberia.
Learners look up rubber plantations in Liberia on Internet.
Learners investigate the main nomadic pastoral areas of Africa and the names of some pastoral groups and create a map of their own to show this.
Learners use Internet to find out about ranching in Botswana.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners’ initial understanding through revision discussions.

Observe learners as they use information from their case studies to discuss and explain: whether Uganda or other countries of Africa should encourage smallholdings or large-scale plantation farming; the best ways of improving smallholder farming in Africa; the advantages and disadvantages of ranching over nomadic pastoral farming in modern Africa; whether better to encourage ranching or the commercialisation of nomadic farming. In conversation, ask learners to use evidence to give reasons for their responses.
Evaluate relevance and accuracy of learners’ conclusions in pair work.
Observe learners’ descriptions and how much information they find from the photograph.
Observe group work and guide groups as necessary.

suggested_uses: Learners find a case study of cocoa farming in Ghana on Internet.
Learners look up rubber plantations in Liberia on Internet.
Learners use Internet to find out about ranching in Botswana.

topic_metadata.topic_title: FORESTS, FOREST RESOURCES AND FORESTRY IN AFRICA

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should understand the importance and uses of forest resources in Africa and the importance of preserving these resources

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know where the main forest resources in Africa are (k)
draw maps to show the areas of the case studies and graphs to illustrate their climates (s)
know the main uses of the forest resources (k)
understand the location and reasons for location of the forest resources in Africa (u)
know the characteristics of the forests in Africa (K)
understand the importance of forests in terms of the environment (u)
understand factors favouring the development of a hardwoods industry (u)
understand the methods of harvesting trees from the forest (u)
understand the development of the hardwood trade in Gabon (u)
identify through photographs the characteristics of forests and activities related to logging in Gabon (s)
present and analyse statistics on the timber industry in Gabon (s, gs)
draw a map showing the major forested areas and timber processing areas in Gabon (s)
appreciate the dangers of unsustainable forestry in Africa and the dangers of destroying forests (a, gs)
form opinions about the dangers of the overuse of the natural vegetation (a)
form opinions about the dangers of overuse of land and water resources and the need to conserve these in the local area
understand the effects of human activity on the landscape (u)

must_cover: The use of forests in Gabon

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners work in groups to research African forests on Internet and identify a list of benefits they bring to the environment, people and the economy.
Learners use their research and present their data to other groups with explanations.
Show photographs of logging and ask learners to describe what they see. In pairs, learners construct a flow diagram to show the production, use and export of timber

Learners work in groups to research deforestation in Africa using the Internet. They use this research and class discussions to help them assume the role of Minister of Forests and report back with a policy to control the cutting down of forests?

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the work they produce to check for accuracy.
Observe as learners explain their findings and make links between the benefits of forests and people’s lives.
Monitor pair work, prompt as necessary. In pair exchange, evaluate how well learners explain their ideas.
In conversation, ask learners to explain the dangers of cutting down forests and suggest how this can be prevented.
Observe learners’ discussions and explanations using their policy reports to identify strategies to control deforestation and make links to impacts on people, environment and economy.

suggested_uses: Learners work in groups to research African forests on Internet
Learners work in groups to research deforestation in Africa using the Internet

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should understand why irrigation is becoming particularly important in African farming, and the methods of small scale and large-scale irrigation.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand how problems of the physical landscape can be overcome with traditional or modern technology (u, a)
recognise physical and other features on conventional survey maps and photographs (s)
draw maps to show the areas of the case studies and graphs to illustrate their climates (s)
know the parts of Africa where irrigation is most important (k)
know some examples of irrigation schemes in Africa (k)
know one example of a large-scale irrigation scheme (k)
understand why irrigation is becoming increasingly important in Africa (u)
understand the factors leading to the development of the Gezira scheme (u)
understand how the Gezira scheme works, its benefits and difficulties (u)
analyse different aspects of the Gezira scheme from statistics and other information (s, gs)
appreciate the advantages of government cooperation with small scale farmers (a, gs)
appreciate the dangers of corruption in government schemes (a, gs)

must_cover: The importance of irrigation and types of irrigation

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners work in pairs or groups to research examples of irrigation schemes and jointly contribute to a class map that has the schemes and their countries labelled.
Learners look up Gezira irrigation scheme on Internet and describe what they find out.
They use information from climate graphs and maps to help them with the context and create their own annotated map to help explain the location.
Learners investigate climate graphs over time and discuss present day issues of climate change. They work in groups to come up with ideas as to how this might affect irrigation in some areas.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Through conversation, check learners’ understanding and their appropriate use of terminology as they respond to initial questions and discuss this as a class.

Learners use their work to suggest whether a large-scale irrigation scheme based on cooperation between local farmers and government would be suitable for Uganda and give their reasons, using evidence.

suggested_uses: Learners look up Gezira irrigation scheme on Internet

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should understand why irrigation is important in China and what methods of irrigation are used.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand how problems of the physical landscape can be overcome with traditional or modern technology (u, a)
draw maps to show the areas of the case studies and graphs to illustrate their climates (s)
know the areas of China where irrigation is important (k)
know the main crops grown on irrigated farms (k)
understand the reasons for the importance of irrigation in China (u)
understand the main methods of irrigation used (u)
understand the principles and use of hydroponics (u)
describe irrigation in China from photographs (s)
appreciate the importance of rice growing and irrigation in China (a, gs)
appreciate what Uganda can learn from rice farming in China and the Gezira scheme (a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Use a series of photographs of the stages of rice growing. Explain these and learners draw a flow diagram to show stages in growing rice (ploughing, flooding field, puddling, planting in nursery, transplanting, weeding, harvesting, threshing, winnowing, drying).
Learners research using Internet to locate key areas of rice growing in China and create their own sketch maps.
They research some facts and images about the rice growing process at different locations, presenting images with flow charts to explain the stages of rice growing.
Learners compare the methods of irrigation used in Gezira and China and suggest which is most suitable for Uganda, giving reasons.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe as learners explain their recommendations for methods of irrigation suitable for Uganda, using evidence from their research and class discussions.

topics.core_competency: After studying this topic, the learner should understand why Switzerland is important for tourism and how this compares with Uganda.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the factors influencing tourism in the selected countries (u)
use statistics, maps and photographs to compare tourism in the selected countries (s)
analyse statistics of tourism in Switzerland (s)
appreciate the contribution of tourism to development (a)
know the major tourist attractions and centres of Switzerland(k)

Learners could create a travel poster for either winter or summer sightseeing, using the main factors that make this place attractive. Working in groups with their posters, each group makes a presentation to the other groups promoting tourism in Switzerland.
Present statistics on the importance of tourism in Switzerland. Ask learners to analyse these to show where the tourists come from and the importance of tourism within the economy.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners’ posters and group presentations to see how well they identify key factors and tourist hot spots. How well do they link location, time of year, climate, landscape and types of activity available?
Learners are asked to compare tourism in Switzerland with tourism in Uganda. They should point out main differences and Similarities.
Ask learners to explain, using their maps/diagrams where tourists come from and the impact on the national economy.

suggested_uses: Learners investigate some of the key tourism areas, using a range of sources including the Internet
